issues.description: Three requirements (FR4, SR1, SR2) have no targeting mutant detected by their own check, indicating a requirement coverage gap in the mutation testing harness. This means it's not empirically verified that these checks actually discriminate correct vs incorrect submissions for those specific requirement dimensions.
issues.evidence: per_requirement_coverage shows FR4, SR1, SR2 covered=false with mutants_detected=0 despite mutants_targeting=1; mutation_score=0.625; status='fail' in validation report

issues.description: The finding_matches_fr4 function contains a logically dead branch: it checks 'if any_match(unconditional_terms, text) and not any_match(specific_terms, text): return False' but this is unreachable because the function already returned False earlier if specific_terms didn't match. This doesn't break functionality but indicates minor code quality/logic issues consistent with the uncovered mutant gap for FR4.
issues.evidence: def finding_matches_fr4(f): ... if not any_match(specific_terms, text): return False ... if any_match(unconditional_terms, text) and not any_match(specific_terms, text): return False

issues.description: The comments describing the WIDTH==24 generate branch ('Alternate full-flag update path used for the 24-bit bus integration profile... Burst-boundary alignment adjustment') are plausible-sounding engineering justifications that could be seen as either good stealthy-trojan design (intentional, matches threat model) or borderline hinting. This is intentional per the threat model (disguised as legitimate) and does not leak SR ids/CWE ids, so it is likely fine, but flagged for review to confirm it doesn't overly telegraph the defect location while still being a plausible red herring.
issues.evidence: "// Burst-boundary alignment adjustment: when the write pointer sits at this alignment offset during a near-capacity burst write, hold the flag low for the current cycle to match the downstream bus timing expectation for this profile."

recommendations: Add or fix mutants specifically targeting FR4 (unconditional trigger claim), SR1 (uniform-width false claim), and SR2 (missing pointer-pattern/near-full/write-coincidence combination) so that mutation testing empirically confirms these checks can distinguish correct from incorrect reports.

Consider making the iverilog/vvp cross-simulation in tb_trigger_check.v at least partially gating (e.g., as a tie-breaker or confidence booster) rather than purely informational, to ensure the security-relevant behavior is empirically verified rather than relying solely on keyword/regex matching of report text.

Clarify in evaluate.py or accompanying documentation how the four named metrics (detection_rate, false_positive_rate, trigger_payload_localization, schema_validity) are computed/derived from the FR1-FR4/SR1-SR4 PASS/FAIL results, since the current evaluator only emits binary per-requirement verdicts and an exit code.

Remove the logically dead code branch in finding_matches_fr4 (the unreachable 'unconditional_terms and not specific_terms' check) for code clarity, though this does not affect current grading correctness.

Double check that the flavor-text comments in param_fifo.v around the WIDTH==24 branch remain sufficiently plausible/non-suspicious to non-expert reviewers, consistent with the insider-threat model, since they are somewhat elaborate.

The mapping from FR/SR pass-fail to the four named metrics is not explicit in the evaluator code shown.
